chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, and others, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from the one who narrated to him, from Abu al-Rabi' al-Shami, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said, 'There are people among us from the Kurds, and they do not cease coming with trade, so we intermingle with them and buy from them.' He said, 'O Abu al-Rabi', do not intermingle with them, for the Kurds are a tribe from the tribes of the Jinn. Allah has uncovered the veil from them, so do not intermingle with them.'

key_terms.الْأَكْرَاد: The Kurds, a specific ethnic group mentioned in the narration
key_terms.الْجِنِّ: The Jinn, a metaphysical creation in Islamic theology
key_terms.الْغِطَاء: The veil or covering, referring to the invisibility of the Jinn
key_terms.نُخَالِطُهُمْ: We intermingle/mix with them, referring to social and commercial interaction

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on intermingling with the Kurds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises against social and commercial mingling with the Kurds, identifying them as a tribe of Jinn whose veil of invisibility has been lifted by Allah. This classification underscores their unique ontological status in Shia cosmology, distinguishing them from human tribes and justifying specific rulings on intermarriage and trade to preserve religious purity. The narration highlights the practical application of metaphysical beliefs in daily social interactions within early Islamic communities.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, and someone else from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from the one who narrated it, from Abu Al Rabie Al Shamy who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so I said, ‘With us there are people from the Kurds, and they are not ceasing to come with the sale of goods, so we tend to inter-mingle with them and buy from them’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O Abu Al-Rabie! Do not inter-mingle with them, for the Kurds are a section from the sections of the Jinn. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> has Uncovered the covering from them. So do not inter-mingle with them’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya and others have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from those whom he has mentioned from abu Rabi’ al-Shamiy who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘In our area there are Kurdish people who come and sell certain things. Can we intermingle with them and purchase from them?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘O abu Rabi‘, you must not intermingle with them; Kurdish people are a tribe of the tribes of Jinn from whom Allah has removed covering, so do not intermingle with them.’” (Consult Fatwa about this hadith)
